newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - April 8.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 8:

WASHINGTON - The White House supplied top-secret information to the Democratic National Committee to block a Latvian business executive with alleged ties to organized crime from attending a dinner with President Bill Clinton.
WASHINGTON - Clinton tried unsuccessfully to jump-start the Mideast peace process during tense talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
WASHINGTON - A Washington Post music critic won a Pulitzer Prize for criticism, while newspapers in Seattle and New Orleans each received two awards.
WASHINGTON - Disabled workers' rights and public safety concerns in the transportation industry may be on a collision course.
WASHINGTON - After the death of Redskins owner Jack Kent Cooke, there are many questions about the future of the team and its new stadium.
VLORE, ALBANIA - The tumultuous popular revolt in Albania has settled into an uneasy stalemate that leaves this little corner of the Balkans almost lawless.
